verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 10% to $9.5B as payments volume grew 9% and cross-border volume 16% in constant dollars, lifting net income 5% to $5.1B.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees from banks for using the Visa brand and network on cards — based on the prior quarter's payments volume.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for clearing and processing each transaction — processed transactions grew 11%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — cross-border volume rose 16% in constant dollars.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services — fraud tools, data and consulting for banks and merchants.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Pay and benefits for Visa's workforce.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Legal provisions, mostly for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case — a charge Visa excludes from its non-GAAP results.

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Network and processing ($207M), professional fees ($143M) and depreciation & amortization ($282M).

follow100Note: Per $100 of gross revenue (before client incentives). Measured against Visa's reported net revenue of $9.5B instead, the kept profit is $53.83 per $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Net revenue hit $9.5B
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 10% to $9.5B — international transactions +14%, data processing +9%, service revenue +8% and other revenue +32%. Payments volume grew 9% and cross-border volume 16% in constant dollars; processed transactions rose 11%.

takeaways.title: Underlying EPS rose 14%
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $2.75, up 14%, and non-GAAP net income $5.5B, up 11%. GAAP EPS rose 8% to $2.58, held back by items Visa excludes, including a $44M litigation provision.

takeaways.title: Incentives keep climbing
takeaways.text: Client incentives — the rebates Visa pays banks and merchants to issue and accept its cards — rose 13% to $3.8B, 29% of gross revenue. Personnel costs jumped 23% to $1.8B, pushing GAAP operating expenses up 22%.

oneTimers: Non-GAAP results exclude the $44M litigation provision, certain acquisition-related amortization and equity-investment losses: non-GAAP net income was $5,463M ($2.75 per share) versus GAAP net income of $5,119M ($2.58).
otherDetail: Interest expense of $182M on Visa's debt, partly offset by $148M of investment income and other income.
footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $9,510M; this page starts from gross revenue of $13,307M so the $3,797M of client incentives shows as a cost.
